learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the capacity for analysis and synthesis.
Acquire the capacity for effective problem-solving.
Acquire skills related to the use of computer programs for calculation, data analysis, and processing within its field of application.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and continuous training.
Develop the capacity for adapting to new situations.
Motivation for quality and continuous improvement.
Knowledge and capacities for the application of materials engineering.
Capacity for managing specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Capacity for interpreting projects and technical reports.
Students must acquire broad knowledge of the different types of materials and their application to engineering.
Students will become familiar with the main joining processes and the problems arising as a consequence of these joints or due to environmental reasons.

syllabus_topics: Theory and practice of non-destructive testing in materials
teaching_methods: Completion of assignments, reports, memoirs and evaluation tests
assessment_rules: For the first call, assessment includes continuous assessment of lab practices (40%), written problem tests (30% with a minimum score of 4/10), and written theory tests (30% with a minimum score of 4/10). For the second call, evaluation consists of a final problem exam (30%, min 4/10), a final theory exam (30%, min 4/10), and a final practical exam (40%, min 4/10). Students in exceptional circumstances may opt for an "exceptional evaluation" consisting of exams identical to the second call tests. The second call of exceptional evaluation allows for the repetition of failed tests.
